concepts.title: Estates System and Privileges of Old Regime France

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Estates System and Privileges of Old Regime France' refers to.
questions.a: French society before 1789 was divided into three social classes where the nobility and clergy enjoyed inherited exemptions from state taxation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Estates System and Privileges of Old Regime France'.
questions.a: Feudal hierarchy exempted upper estates while burdening commoners with state taxes.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Estates System and Privileges of Old Regime France' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1 (source: iess301.txt lines 85-125)

questions.q: Calculate the tithe payable on an agricultural produce of {produce} quintals. Use the method 'Calculation of Tithe Tax'. Work with: produce = 360. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of tithe.
questions.a: 36 units

questions.q: Find the church tax tithe when the total harvest is {produce} kg. Use the method 'Calculation of Tithe Tax'. Work with: produce = 240. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of tithe.
questions.a: 24 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Calculation of Tithe Tax' refers to.
questions.a: The church in Old Regime France levied an agricultural tax called tithe, which equaled one-tenth of the total crop harvested by peasants.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Calculation of Tithe Tax'.
questions.a: Tithe represents a direct 10 percent levy on agrarian yield collected by the clergy.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Calculation of Tithe Tax', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: tithe = produce / 10

concepts.title: Causes and Mechanism of Subsistence Crisis

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Causes and Mechanism of Subsistence Crisis' refers to.
questions.a: An extreme economic situation in Old Regime France where rapid population growth outpaced grain production, leading to soaring bread prices and widespread starvation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Causes and Mechanism of Subsistence Crisis'.
questions.a: Mismatch between population growth and food supply triggers escalating scarcity and mortality.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Causes and Mechanism of Subsistence Crisis' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1.1 (source: iess301.txt lines 140-165)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Influence of Enlightenment Philosophers' refers to.
questions.a: Ideas proposed by Locke, Rousseau, and Montesquieu challenged divine monarchical right, proposing social contracts and division of government powers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Influence of Enlightenment Philosophers'.
questions.a: Enlightenment philosophy articulated equality, popular sovereignty, and separation of powers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Influence of Enlightenment Philosophers' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1.3 (source: iess301.txt lines 170-220)

concepts.title: Convocation of Estates General and Voting Rights Conflict

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Convocation of Estates General and Voting Rights Conflict' refers to.
questions.a: The assembly representing all three estates called on 5 May 1789, where dispute over voting by order versus individual voting led to Third Estate walkout.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Convocation of Estates General and Voting Rights Conflict'.
questions.a: Refusal of individual voting rights sparked political rebellion by Third Estate representatives.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Convocation of Estates General and Voting Rights Conflict' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2 (source: iess301.txt lines 225-265)

concepts.title: Tennis Court Oath and Outbreak of Revolution

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Tennis Court Oath and Outbreak of Revolution' refers to.
questions.a: The Third Estate declared itself the National Assembly on 20 June 1789 at Versailles, swearing to draft a constitution limiting royal power.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Tennis Court Oath and Outbreak of Revolution'.
questions.a: Self-declaration as National Assembly and Tennis Court Oath marked the formal shift away from absolutism.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Tennis Court Oath and Outbreak of Revolution' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2 (source: iess301.txt lines 260-310)

questions.q: Calculate the minimum tax required to become an active citizen if the daily wage is {daily_wage} livres. Use the method 'Active Citizen Voting Threshold Computation'. Work with: daily_wage = 50. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of min_tax.
questions.a: 150 units

questions.q: Find the tax threshold for voting rights when a labourer earns {daily_wage} livres per day. Use the method 'Active Citizen Voting Threshold Computation'. Work with: daily_wage = 50. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of min_tax.
questions.a: 150 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Active Citizen Voting Threshold Computation' refers to.
questions.a: Under the 1791 Constitution, voting rights were granted only to men above 25 who paid direct tax equal to at least three days of a worker's wage.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Active Citizen Voting Threshold Computation'.
questions.a: Financial threshold for active citizenship required tax equivalent to three days of manual labor wages.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Active Citizen Voting Threshold Computation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: min_tax = 3 * daily_wage

concepts.title: Rights of Man and Political Symbolism

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Rights of Man and Political Symbolism' refers to.
questions.a: The 1791 Constitution incorporated natural inalienable rights alongside visual political symbols to convey revolutionary values to an illiterate populace.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Rights of Man and Political Symbolism'.
questions.a: Declaration enshrined natural rights while allegorical symbols communicated liberty, equality, and unity.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Rights of Man and Political Symbolism' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2.1 (source: iess301.txt lines 340-410)

concepts.title: Jacobin Club, Sans-Culottes, and Establishment of Republic

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Jacobin Club, Sans-Culottes, and Establishment of Republic' refers to.
questions.a: Political radicalization led by Robespierre's Jacobins (sans-culottes) resulted in the storming of Tuileries, ending monarchy and creating the Republic in 1792.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Jacobin Club, Sans-Culottes, and Establishment of Republic'.
questions.a: Radical lower-class mobilization replaced constitutional monarchy with a elected republic.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Jacobin Club, Sans-Culottes, and Establishment of Republic' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3 (source: iess301.txt lines 415-485)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Reign of Terror under Robespierre' refers to.
questions.a: The period from 1793 to 1794 characterized by Robespierre's harsh policies of state control, price ceilings, rationing, and execution by guillotine.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Reign of Terror under Robespierre'.
questions.a: State control and violent suppression of perceived political enemies defined the Reign of Terror.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Reign of Terror under Robespierre' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.1 (source: iess301.txt lines 480-530)

concepts.title: Role and Demands of Women in the Revolution

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Role and Demands of Women in the Revolution' refers to.
questions.a: Women actively participated in revolution through political clubs like the Society of Revolutionary and Republican Women, demanding equal voting and civil rights.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Role and Demands of Women in the Revolution'.
questions.a: Women fought for civil and political rights, facing suppression under the Terror before securing suffrage in 1946.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Role and Demands of Women in the Revolution' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 4 (source: iess301.txt lines 550-630)

concepts.title: Triangular Slave Trade and Abolition in French Colonies

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Triangular Slave Trade and Abolition in French Colonies' refers to.
questions.a: A maritime commercial network connecting Europe, Africa, and Americas to supply plantation commodities, abolished by Convention in 1794 and permanently in 1848.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Triangular Slave Trade and Abolition in French Colonies'.
questions.a: Port prosperity relied on forced labor until colonial slavery was legally eradicated.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Triangular Slave Trade and Abolition in French Colonies' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 5 (source: iess301.txt lines 635-680)
